quote: MCSPlayer.as:210 'if(StatsManager.hasBuff(StatsManager.BUFF_ATTACK))' :212 'this.minDamage *= 1.5;' · :191 'this.minDamage = minDamage;' :192 'this.damageRange = damageRange;' · :3201 'var baseDamage:int = this.minDamage + Math.random() * this.damageRange;'  ||  web §1t99s0§.as:211-213 same three lines under the obfuscated buff test
text: BUFF_ATTACK does not multiply damage by 1.5 - it multiplies the minDamage FLOOR by 1.5 and leaves damageRange untouched. Damage rolls as minDamage + random()*damageRange, so under the buff the expected damage rises by 1.5*minDamage - minDamage, i.e. strictly LESS than a 1.5x total unless damageRange is zero. Consequence for the contaminated duel_dense footage: it is inflated, but 'divide by 1.5' is the wrong correction and would under-report the true TTK. The same is true of BUFF_INJURED (x0.5 on minDamage and defense and baseSlashLength) and BUFF_DEFENSE (x1.5 on defense only).

text: InputManager.maxDistance = 200 is a compile-time initialiser, not a gameplay base. setStance calls InputManager.setMaxDistance(slashLength) on every battle init for the local player (web §1t99s0§.as:3156-3158, android MCSPlayer.as:3092-3094), so the 200 is overwritten before the player ever draws a stroke. Any derivation of the wiki's 300/200/100 that treats 200 as 'the shipped default slash budget' rests on a value the player never plays at. The real base is 120 + floor((90 + 5*DAN) * SPD / (20 + SPD)) — 124 at SPD 1 / dan 0, asymptotically 210 at dan 0.

Payload: baseSlashLength = 120 + Math.floor((90 + Dan*5) * speed / (20 + speed)); slashModifier Light 1.5 / Balanced 1+0.005m / Heavy 0.5+0.005m.
